identity.title: Transformative or Conservative? Conservation laws for ResNets and Transformers

problem.claim: The paper studies conservation laws in gradient-flow training dynamics for practical architectures, including ResNets and Transformers.

gap.claim: Conservation laws were well understood mainly for shallow ReLU and linear networks, but remained largely unexplored for more practical architectures.

contributions.claim: Characterizes conservation laws for basic shallow ReLU and linear networks, with or without convolution, and for a single attention layer.
Introduces subset-parameter conservation laws and reduces their characterization to analyzing the corresponding building block in isolation.
Examines whether the identified conservation principles persist under discrete optimization, especially SGD, after being established in continuous gradient flow.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce conservation laws depending only on a subset of parameters, such as consecutive layers, residual blocks, or attention layers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that basic shallow ReLU and linear networks have easily expressed conservation laws and no more than the previously known ones.
The authors report a complete description of all conservation laws for a single attention layer, and that residual blocks have the same conservation laws as their nonskip counterparts.
The authors report examining persistence of these principles under discrete dynamics, particularly SGD; the abstract does not state the resulting conditions or findings.

narrative_sequence.summary: Identifies the limited understanding of conservation laws beyond mostly shallow ReLU and linear networks.
Characterizes laws for shallow ReLU and linear building blocks, including convolutional variants.
Describes all laws for a single attention layer and relates residual-block laws to blocks without skip connections.
Defines subset-parameter conservation laws and reduces their study to isolated building blocks.
Investigates persistence under discrete optimization, especially SGD.

source_observation.claim: The abstract moves from whole architectures to conservation laws localized to parameter subsets, then reduces their analysis to isolated building blocks.

lessons.interpretation: Localizing a structural claim can make complex-architecture analysis tractable while preserving a clear link to components.
lessons.application: For a modular architecture, formulate invariants over one block or parameter subset first, and state the reduction connecting that local analysis to the full model.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the property fundamentally depends on cross-block interactions that cannot be isolated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the mathematical form of the conservation laws or the assumptions under which the characterizations hold.
The reported SGD persistence analysis lacks its concrete conditions and conclusions.
The abstract does not quantify the scope of the architectures or optimization settings examined.
